method: Sequential builds of one external native-runtime embedding probe against frozen Core extraction source. Separate private targets and Kache runtime/configuration per arm, shared object store, identical final probe and profile, KACHE_ADAPTIVE_INCREMENTAL=0. Only HARN_BUILD_REVISION changes between measured rebuilds.

identity_control.probe: Install harn-stdlib, construct the native VM, read runtime_content_fingerprint(), require source_revision == expected and a nonempty content_sha256.

interpretation: Retained private incremental state roughly halves revision-only rebuild time in this probe. This is not a merge-group result or an adoption decision for ephemeral targets, source edits, test compilation, or every compiler profile.
limitations: Two rebuilds per arm, incremental first and artifact-only second, on a shared host. Dependencies are warm for both measured rebuild pairs; the arms were not interleaved.

The first incremental build compiled successfully but its original identity probe omitted runtime initialization and panicked. Adding the native VM alone still omitted explicit stdlib installation. Both failed probes and repair logs are retained; the corrected probe verified the seed before measured rebuilds. Initial seed timings are excluded from the rebuild comparison.

Kache reports are cumulative per checkout session, not per build. Counter deltas require the same non-null session identity. The incremental session starts at the final probe repair, so it does not describe the original seed compilation.

The incremental native compilation appears as a passthrough and its compiler time is absent from Kache's cache timing total. Wall-clock measurements and Cargo compiler-unit sections establish the rebuild times.
A real source edit, the canonical CLI link, test units, storage growth, and hosted archive restoration remain unmeasured by this experiment. CI configuration is unchanged by this record.
